questions.q: Why is sound called a mechanical wave?
questions.a: It needs a material medium of particles vibrating to carry energy; it cannot travel in vacuum.
Compressions are regions of crowded high-pressure particles; rarefactions are spread-out low-pressure regions.

questions.q: In which direction do particles vibrate in a sound wave?
questions.a: Along the direction of wave travel - sound is longitudinal.

solution_steps.name: period_s

concepts.title: Reflection of Sound: Echo and Reverberation

questions.a: A reflected sound heard distinctly after the original, needing about 17 m distance for a 0.1 s gap.
Repeated multiple reflections that prolong sound in big halls; soft materials on walls reduce it.

questions.q: State two uses of sound reflection.
questions.a: Megaphones, stethoscopes and sonar - all direct or use reflected sound.

concepts.title: Range of Hearing and Ultrasound Applications

questions.q: What is the range of hearing of humans?
What is ultrasound and name one use?
questions.a: Sound above 20 kHz - used in sonar, medical imaging and cleaning delicate parts.

questions.q: Which animals use ultrasound to navigate?
questions.a: Bats and dolphins emit ultrasound and judge distance from the echoes.
